slides.0.title: Icewine, Sparkling and Style
slides.0.subtitle: Icewine rules and style, sparkling wine and tasting cues
slides.1.title: The icewine style
slides.1.highlights.0.title: How icewine is made
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Grapes must freeze naturally on the vine and be harvested below -8°C, with juice of at least 35°Brix; VQA icewine must be 100% icewine with the viticultural area on the front label (VQA Ontario). BC also requires pressing while frozen and at least 100 g/L residual sugar at bottling (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Main grapes
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Vidal is the mainstay, with icewines also made from Riesling, Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon (Wikipedia); Vidal made about 83% of Ontario icewine in 2025–26 (388,970 of 468,752 litres, Wine With Seth)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: The first icewine vintage
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Sources differ: Wikipedia says Inniskillin first tried in 1983 and Pelee Island Winery succeeded that year, while Winealign says Karl Kaiser harvested Inniskillin's first Vidal icewine in 1984. It is not tested
slides.1.content: Icewine is among the most tightly regulated VQA categories.
slides.2.title: Other VQA sweet and special categories
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Late-harvest tiers
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Late Harvest needs at least 22°Brix, Select Late Harvest 26, Special Select Late Harvest 30 and icewine 35; Botrytized and Totally Botrytized wines are separate categories. All of these must show a vintage (VQA Ontario)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Appassimento and skin-fermented white
slides.2.highlights.1.content: The term Appassimento may be used for wines that are at least 85% dried grapes; wines with 15–85% dried grapes may say "Appassimento-method" if the exact percentage is declared. Skin Fermented White must spend at least 10 days on skins and be declared on the front label (VQA Ontario)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Residual sugar figures
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Wikipedia gives roughly 180–320 g/L residual sugar for Ontario icewine, while BC's floor is 100 g/L (Wine With Seth). These are different thresholds under different rules and the former is single-source, so neither is tested
slides.2.content: Sweet-wine tiers are set by sugar at harvest.
slides.3.title: Sparkling wine and tasting cues
slides.3.highlights.0.title: VQA sparkling
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Sparkling needs pressure of not less than 300 kPa from secondary fermentation, with natural carbonation; Effervescent wine has pressure no greater than 300 kPa and follows table-wine labelling rules (VQA Ontario). Ontario's traditional-method sparkling mostly uses Chardonnay and Pinot Noir, and the cool climate and limestone-based soils of Niagara and Prince Edward County are often compared with Champagne (Wine With Seth, Glass of Bubbly)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Style cues by origin
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Niagara bench wines are often described as mineral, linked to the dolomites beneath; Prince Edward County's Pinot Noir and Chardonnay are likewise known for minerality (Wine With Seth, VQA Ontario); Nova Scotia whites show bright, steely acidity, restrained alcohol and aromatic freshness (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Okanagan cues
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Southern summer afternoons of 30–35°C with 15–20°C diurnal swings (Wine With Seth) give riper reds such as Syrah and Bordeaux varieties, while the cooler centre and north lean to aromatic whites and Pinot Noir
slides.3.content: The cues are minerality, acidity and south-to-north ripeness.
